contexts.context_exact: \begin{abstract}Dealers set limits on the largest absolute position reached before a review horizon ends. We compare conditional quantile forecasts with historical rules using an hourly FX record, its daily aggregates and weekly dealer positions. Simple historical rules are hard to beat. Long-history FX regression lowers matched loss by 14.8\% and 16.6\% across periods. Delayed calibration retains the later gain (15.0\%), with 329 versus 328 breaches. Rankings against a shorter rolling rule vary by period. Expanded regularization leaves regression behind in 34 of 48 weekly panel comparisons, and historical rules win most daily comparisons. Stationary controlled simulations already produce large short-history losses. In newly calibrated simulations at history 52, the full regression's median loss increase across series is 116.2\% under constant parameters and 121.4\% under parameter switching. The mechanism behind the observed low-frequency losses remains unidentified. Peak-limit validation should assess accuracy, breaches and reference stability together.\end{abstract}

contexts.context_exact: Further comparisons apply delayed calibration, fixed combinations and conservative selection to the same peak response. A headroom CAViaR recursion and calibration wrappers follow existing methods \citep{engle2004,gibbs2021}. Calibration parameters update after outcomes mature. Fixed mean and median combinations use predefined members. Conservative selection favors the strongest shrinkage within one paired HAC standard error of the validation winner. This adapts one-standard-error selection \citep{hastie2009} to paired forecast losses.
